title: Design and Implementation of MPI-Native GPU-Initiated MPI Partitioned Communication
problem: MPI lacks explicit GPU support mechanisms, making it difficult to efficiently deploy message-passing communication on GPU-accelerated systems. Vendor-specific libraries like NCCL and RCCL provide efficient GPU-Initiated Communication but use non-standard semantics not available in MPI.
motivation: GPU-accelerated HPC systems require standardized, efficient GPU-Initiated communication patterns, but MPI has not yet defined explicit mechanisms for this capability.
method: The authors extend MPI 4.0's Partitioned Point-to-Point communication to support Intra-Kernel GPU-Initiated Communication and Partitioned Collectives, enabling GPUs to trigger persistent communication channels. The implementation incorporates techniques from vendor-specific libraries like NCCL and NVSHMEM. Evaluation uses NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper systems testing on NVLink and InfiniBand networks with Jacobi solver and Deep Learning Kernel benchmarks.
key_novelty: Extension of MPI Partitioned communication to enable GPU-Initiated intra-kernel communication and Partitioned Collectives, standardizing vendor-specific GPU communication patterns within MPI.
contributions: Extended MPI Partitioned Point-to-Point communication for GPU-Initiated intra-kernel communication
Incorporated techniques from NCCL and NVSHMEM into MPI framework
Demonstrated benefits on NVIDIA GH200 with NVLink and InfiniBand networks

metrics.other: Benefits of GPU-Initiated communication evaluated on application kernels; specific speedup metrics not provided in abstract

limitations: Evaluation scope limited to NVIDIA GH200 systems; broader hardware portability not discussed in abstract.
